materiality_analysis.reason: The 2024 disclosure defines the six specific account types (e.g., separately managed, unified managed) that generate wealth management revenues. Removing this definition obscures the structural breakdown of the revenue-generating asset base. Investors rely on this to assess the mix of advisory fees vs. transactional fees and the potential impact of fee compression or client behavior shifts. The removal of this operational definition is a meaningful change in the disclosure of the business model's nuances.

comparisons.peer_topic: Asset and Wealth Management services overview
comparisons.peer_summary: The Asset & Wealth Management segment provides investment services to institutional and individual clients globally, managing assets across equity, fixed income, and alternative investments through various structures like mutual funds and separately managed accounts.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS disclose that asset management revenues or services are generated through various account structures, specifically highlighting separately managed accounts as a key vehicle. MS explicitly lists 'separately managed-accounts' as a primary source of asset management revenue where third-party and affiliated asset managers make investment decisions. Similarly, GS identifies 'separately managed accounts' as one of the structures in which it offers investment solutions to clients, alongside mutual funds and private partnerships.

sentences.text: Asset management revenues within the Wealth Management segment are primarily generated from the following types of accounts:

• Separately managed-accounts by which third party and affiliated asset managers are engaged to manage clients' assets with investment decisions made by the asset manager. Only one third-party asset manager strategy can be held per account.
We manage client assets across a broad range of investment strategies and asset classes, including equity, fixed income and alternative investments.
We offer our investment solutions in a variety of structures, including separately managed accounts, mutual funds, private partnerships and other commingled vehicles.
